notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup (free tier). Product: chat-based customer support assistant (SaaS). Early discovery call 2026-03-05 — technical PM + engineering lead attended. Primary problem: unpredictable traffic spikes from scheduled batch customer imports and marketing-driven bursts (webhook fanout). They saw multiple 429s when we throttled their demo, causing failures in message ingestion and unhappy QA.

Key quotes: "We want something that 'just survives' spikes without losing messages — not great if 20% of users see errors on Mondays." — PM.

Requirements notes (shorthand):
- Workload: chat sessions + doc search fallback. High concurrency for short bursts (10s of seconds).
- Targets: P95 latency < 300ms for chat token generation during normal traffic; tolerate higher in bursts but want graceful degradation.
- Throughput: typical steady-state 20 req/s, burst to 400 req/s for ~2–5 minutes on campaigns.
- Cost sensitivity: high — SMB budget, needs predictable tiers.
- Model preference: open Llama2-variants / smaller hosted families; willing to try quantized weights.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper model or cached responses when limits hit.

Security/compliance: SOC2 ok, SSO/SAML for admin portal, audit logs for admin actions. Data residency not required (US cloud ok).

Notes on current infra: using single-region AWS, stateless front end, currently rate-limits per API key implemented in app layer; experiencing accidental double-throttling when Redwood limits + app limits both apply.

Ask: clear guidance and defaults for hosted_api quotas, a recommended backoff strategy, ability to request temporary burst credit for onboarding, documentation for concurrency vs qps, webhooks on 429 and webhook retry semantics.

Sales context: small ARR potential if self-serve converts; could expand to Dedicated later if they sign >$20k ARR. Keep motion lightweight — prefer async tech touch.

Next steps: propose rate-limit config (soft limit + burst window), send sample client-side exponential backoff with jitter, schedule follow-up 30m tech call 2026-03-17.
